question: A tomato sauce holding 0.6 mg of iron per 100 g simmers in an unenamelled cast-iron pot. Roughly how much iron afterwards?
answer: About 6 mg, roughly ten times as much. Acid in the tomatoes dissolves iron from the pot wall during a long simmer. In a 1986 US test, spaghetti sauce rose from about 0.6 to nearly 6 mg per 100 g. One serving then carries a good share of an adult's daily iron.
move: A container can be an ingredient; ask what it gives up.
trap: About 0.7 mg, as a seasoned pot seems to add almost nothing.

diagram.caption: The pot gave up about ten times the iron the sauce began with.

source: Brittin & Nossaman, J. Am. Diet. Assoc., 1986
reference: Brittin & Nossaman, Iron content of food cooked in iron utensils, Journal of the American Dietetic Association 86, 897, 1986
